arxiv-1801-08529.title: Fuchsian Equations with Three Non-Apparent Singularities
arxiv-1801-08529.creator: Alexandre EREMENKO † and Vitaly TARASOV ‡§
arxiv-1801-08529.description: Abstract We show that for every second order Fuchsian linear differential equation E E with n n singularities of which n − 3 n-3 are apparent there exists a hypergeometric equation H H and a linear differential operator with polynomial coefficients which maps the space of solutions of H H into the space of solutions of E E .

arxiv-2012-06962.title: Microfluidic device coupled with total internal reflection microscopy for in situ observation of precipitation
arxiv-2012-06962.creator: Jia Meng, Jae Bem You, Gilmar F. Arends, Hao Hao, Xiaoli Tan and Xuehua Zhang
arxiv-2012-06962.description: Abstract In situ observation of precipitation or phase separation induced by solvent addition is important in studying its dynamics. Combined with optical and fluorescence microscopy, microfluidic devices have been leveraged in studying the phase separation in various materials including biominerals, nanoparticles, and inorganic crystals.

arxiv-2012-11108.title: Classical and quantum exact solutions for a FRW in chiral like cosmology
arxiv-2012-11108.creator: J. Socorro, S. Pérez-Payán, Rafael Hernández-Jiménez, Abraham Espinoza-García, Luis Rey Díaz-Barrón
arxiv-2012-11108.description: Abstract In this work, first, we study a flat Friedmann-Robertson-Walker Universe with two scalar fields but only one potential term, which can be thought as a simple quintessence plus a K-essence model. Employing the Hamiltonian formalism we are able to obtain the classical and quantum solutions.

arxiv-2305-09072.title: Skin Deep: Investigating Subjectivity in Skin Tone Annotations for Computer Vision Benchmark Datasets Conference: 2023 ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency; June 12–15, 2023; Chicago, IL, USA 2023 ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency (FAccT ’23), June

arxiv-2305-09072.description: Abstract . To investigate the well-observed racial disparities in computer vision systems that analyze images of humans, researchers have turned to skin tone as more objective annotation than race metadata for fairness performance evaluations. However, the current state of skin tone annotation procedures is highly varied.

arxiv-2308-07682.title: 60 years of cyclic monotonicity: a survey
arxiv-2308-07682.creator: L. De Pascale, A. Kausamo, K. Wyczesany
arxiv-2308-07682.description: Abstract Dedicated to Prof. R. T. Rockafellar in occasion of his 90th birthday. 1 Aims and scopes The primary purpose of this note is to provide an instructional summary of the state of the art regarding cyclic monotonicity and related notions.

arxiv-2311-17946.title: DreamSync: Aligning Text-to-Image Generation with Image Understanding Feedback
arxiv-2311-17946.creator: Jiao Sun Deqing Fu Yushi Hu Su Wang Royi RassinDa-Cheng Juan Dana Alon Charles Herrmann Sjoerd van SteenkisteRanjay Krishna Cyrus Rashtchian University of Southern California University of Washington Bar-Ilan UniversityGoogle Research
arxiv-2311-17946.description: Abstract Despite their wide-spread success, Text-to-Image models (T2I) still struggle to produce images that are both aesthetically pleasing and faithful to the user’s input text. We introduce DreamSync , a model-agnostic training algorithm by design that improves T2I models to be faithful to the text input.

arxiv-2312-07610.title: Interpretational errors in statistical causal inference
arxiv-2312-07610.creator: Aaron L. Sarvet, Mats J. Stensrud, Lan Wen
arxiv-2312-07610.description: Abstract We formalize an interpretational error that is common in statistical causal inference, termed identity slippage . This formalism is used to describe historically-recognized fallacies, and analyse a fast-growing literature in statistics and applied fields. We conducted a systematic review of natural language claims in the literature on stochastic mediation parameters, and documented extensive evidence of identity slippage in applications.

arxiv-2403-18750.title: Full counting statistics of 1d short-range Riesz gases in confinement
arxiv-2403-18750.creator: Grégory Schehr
arxiv-2403-18750.description: Abstract We investigate the full counting statistics (FCS) of a harmonically confined 1d short-range Riesz gas consisting of N N particles in equilibrium at finite temperature. The particles interact with each other through a repulsive power-law interaction with an exponent k > 1 k>1 which includes the Calogero-Moser model for k = 2 k=2 .

arxiv-2404-09816.title: FedP3: Federated Personalized and Privacy-friendly Network Pruning under Model Heterogeneity
arxiv-2404-09816.creator: Kai Yi, Nidham Gazagnadou, Peter Richtárik, Lingjuan Lyu
arxiv-2404-09816.description: Abstract The interest in federated learning has surged in recent research due to its unique ability to train a global model using privacy-secured information held locally on each client. This paper pays particular attention to the issue of client-side model heterogeneity, a pervasive challenge in the practical implementation of FL that escalates its complexity.

arxiv-2405-16967.title: Imaginary past of a quantum particle moving on imaginary time
arxiv-2405-16967.creator: A. Uranga 1,2, E. Akhmatskaya 1,3, D. Sokolovski 2,3
arxiv-2405-16967.description: Abstract The analytical continuation of classical equations of motion to complex times suggests that a tunnelling particle spends in the barrier an imaginary duration i ​ | 𝒯 | i|{\mathcal{T}}| . Does this mean that it takes a finite time to tunnel, or should tunnelling be seen as an instantaneous process?

arxiv-2502-08636.title: Spatial457: A Diagnostic Benchmark for 6D Spatial Reasoning of Large Multimodal Models
arxiv-2502-08636.creator: Xingrui Wang, Wufei Ma, Tiezheng Zhang, Celso M de Melo, Jieneng Chen, Alan Yuille
arxiv-2502-08636.description: Abstract Although large multimodal models (LMMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in visual scene interpretation and reasoning, their capacity for complex and precise 3-dimensional spatial reasoning remains uncertain. Existing benchmarks focus predominantly on 2D spatial understanding and lack a framework to comprehensively evaluate 6D spatial reasoning across varying complexities.

arxiv-2511-22175.title: 2D MoS 2 /Au interfaces for enhanced opto-electronic response with sub-bandgap photons
arxiv-2511-22175.creator: J. Zhong, K. J. Karki
arxiv-2511-22175.description: Abstract Monolayer MoS 2 is a direct band gap semiconductor with potential applications in optoelectronics and photonics. MoS 2 also has a large optical nonlinearity. However, the atomic thickness of the monolayer limits the strength of the measured functional signals, such as the photocurrent or photoluminescence, in optoelectronic devices.

pmc-10751513.title: Effect of diet low in advanced glycation end products on appetite, body composition, and brown adipose tissue markers in patients with coronary artery disease treated with angioplasty: A randomized controlled trial
pmc-10751513.creator: Fatemeh Taheri, Ali Vasheghani-Farahani, Elaheh Honarkar-Shafie, Hamidreza Poorhosseini, Mehdi Yaseri, Mohammad Javad Hosseinzadeh-Attar
pmc-10751513.description: Background:Recent changes in dietary habits have resulted in increased intake of advanced glycation end products (AGEs), which are known to have a predominant contribution to the pathogenesis and complications of coronary artery disease (CAD). AGEs are also thought to induce weight gain by affecting appetite, energy expenditure, and brown adipose tissue (BAT).

pmc-11354025.title: Trends in Physiotherapy of Chronic Low Back Pain Research: Knowledge Synthesis Based on Bibliometric Analysis
pmc-11354025.creator: Urška Šajnović, Peter Kokol, Jernej Završnik, Helena Blažun Vošner, Daniele Giansanti
pmc-11354025.description: Background: Physiotherapy and chronic low back pain (CLBP) form a broad and quickly developing research area. The aim of this article was to holistically, thematically and chronologically analyze and synthesize the literature production in this research area and identify the most prolific research entities and research themes.

pmc-11425518.title: 68 6200-6700 steps per day are associated with better health and wellbeing among working-aged adults a
pmc-11425518.creator: Pauliina Husu, Henri Vähä-Ypyä, Kari Tokola, Harri Sievänen, Tommi Vasankari
pmc-11425518.description: PurposePhysical activity (PA) is important for health and wellbeing, and the number of steps is one indicator of ambulatory PA. Guidelines of PA needed for health and wellbeing exist, but the adequate number of daily steps is equivocal. This study aimed at identifying potential step cut-points for selected indicators of health and wellbeing.

pmc-11582679.title: Single-cell electro-mechanical shear flow deformability cytometry
pmc-11582679.creator: Junyu Chen, Xueping Zou, Daniel C Spencer, Hywel Morgan
pmc-11582679.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). We have developed a microfluidic technique that exploits non-contact shear flow deformability cytometry to simultaneously characterise both the electrical and mechanical properties of single cells at high speed.

pmc-12413008.title: RETRACTED: HGLER: A hierarchical heterogeneous graph networks for enhanced multimodal emotion recognition in conversations

pmc-12644819.title: Structural basis of lipopolysaccharide assembly by the outer membrane translocon holo-complex
pmc-12644819.creator: Haoxiang Chen, Axel Siroy, Violette Morales, Dominik Gurvič, Yves Quentin, Stephanie Balor, Yassin A Abuta’a, Maurine Marteau, Carine Froment, Anne Caumont-Sarcos, Julien Marcoux, Phillip J Stansfeld, Rémi Fronzes, Raffaele Ieva
pmc-12644819.description: Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) assembly at the surfaces-exposed leaflet of the bacterial outer membrane (OM) is mediated by the OM LPS translocon. An essential transmembrane β-barrel protein, LptD, and a cognate lipoprotein, LptE, translocate LPS selectively into the OM external leaflet via a poorly understood mechanism. Here, we characterize two additional translocon subunits, the lipoproteins LptM and LptY (formerly YedD).
